# SHARED SCALAR / CARRIER CORPUS (task 1.5-h).
#
# FIVE BOUNDS, EIGHT SITES. A BOUND is the frozen ceiling; a SITE is an independently
# removable gate. The five are MaxPolicyIDBytes, MaxPrincipalBytes, MaxPlanHeaderBytes,
# MaxTraceStrBytes and MaxReasonBytes; each runtime asserts the DISTINCT SET, not just a count,
# so adding a row under a sixth bound cannot slip in as one more site of an existing one. `MaxPolicyIDBytes` and `MaxPrincipalBytes` are BOTH 128 and stay SEPARATE
# NAMED BOUNDS: they bound different quantities and either may move alone, so collapsing them
# would make one bound's drift invisible behind the other's rows.
#
# A LOWER BOUND NEEDS TWO CONTROLS, NOT ONE. SEVEN of the eight sites are SEMANTICALLY
# two-sided -- they admit 1..Max, whatever spelling the gate uses -- which freezes a MINIMUM OF
# 1 as well as a ceiling, and a zero-refusal alone does not pin it. A validator tightened to reject length 1 refuses zero exactly as before, so the
# `min` column carries the SMALLEST ADMISSIBLE VALUE and each runtime asserts it is ACCEPTED.
# FOUR controls per two-sided site: zero refused, min accepted, at accepted, over refused.
# The lower pair is needed AT EACH SITE, not once per helper: a helper-level test proves the
# helper's arithmetic, not that a given carrier still routes through it.
#
# `plan_header_raw` is ONE-SIDED -- a raw byte ceiling with no minimum -- so `zero` and `min`
# are `n/a`. It carries at/over plus a STAGE WITNESS instead, because a raw ceiling's
# pre-decode ordering is not something an at/over pair can show.
#
# `abort_reason` carries SIX: the four above apply when the kind is ABORTED, and a non-ABORTED
# event must carry NO reason -- a separate, independently removable predicate needing its own
# ACCEPTED (empty) and REFUSED (non-empty) control. Without the accepted one, a predicate
# refusing every non-aborted event would satisfy the refusal.
#
# `tombstone_reason_signed` carries the four, on the signed recovery-control path.
#
# Both runtimes now enforce all three principal sites, including the raw record boundary.
# Lifecycle abort reasons also have both peers; remaining n/a rows name their owner.
#
# THE LITERALS ARE STATED HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE. Deriving `over` from the production constant
# would move every row with the bound, so a ceiling drifting to 64 or 4096 would keep the whole
# corpus green. Each runtime asserts its constant against these values -- and where a runtime
# keeps the ceiling private, it proves the value behaviourally rather than exposing a
# test-only accessor.
#
# VERDICT COLUMNS are per runtime, for the OVER case. `n/a` means that runtime has no peer for
# the site; `owner` names who owns building one, so an absent peer is a recorded gap and never
# a silent exemption.
#
# NOT A SITE: the plan RANGE availability-policy length. It was a derived arm -- a range must
# EQUAL the header's already-bounded policy, so no input reached its length arm alone -- and it
# SHADOWED the header's own proof, refusing a consistent over-limit policy with the header
# bound deleted. The bound is now CENTRALIZED at the header and the range is equality-only.
#
# site                        bound                 zero    min  at      over    go      elixir  owner
policy_plan_header            MaxPolicyIDBytes      refuse  1    128     129     refuse  refuse  -
policy_assignment_record      MaxPolicyIDBytes      refuse  1    128     129     refuse  refuse  -
principal_producer_context    MaxPrincipalBytes     refuse  1    128     129     refuse  refuse  -
principal_edge_slot           MaxPrincipalBytes     refuse  1    128     129     refuse  refuse  -
principal_service_slot        MaxPrincipalBytes     refuse  1    128     129     refuse  refuse  -
plan_header_raw               MaxPlanHeaderBytes    n/a     n/a  524288  524289  refuse  refuse  -
abort_reason                  MaxTraceStrBytes      refuse  1    256     257     refuse  refuse  -
tombstone_reason_signed       MaxReasonBytes        refuse  1    256     257     refuse  n/a     1.6-d
